title: Evri parcel-delivery phishing with authoritative DNS on sanctioned Aeza
summary: A parcel-delivery (Evri) phishing domain runs its own authoritative nameservers inside the OFAC-sanctioned bulletproof host Aeza, while serving the phishing page from commodity hosting — using the sanctioned operator for DNS resilience against takedown.
detail: delivery-evriupdate[.]live impersonates the UK parcel courier Evri. VirusTotal flags it 10/94 malicious and categorises it as phishing. Its nameservers ns1/ns2[.]delivery-evriupdate[.]live both resolve to 77[.]221[.]156[.]75, an IP announced by AS210644 (AEZA-AS, Aeza Group LLC — OFAC-sanctioned), while the phishing web content is served from 192[.]64[.]119[.]19 (Namecheap). Hosting only the DNS on the sanctioned bulletproof operator, with the disposable web page on commodity hosting, is a takedown-resilience pattern.
